steps.message: Building SimpleApp.csproj and attaching a binlog with dotnet build SimpleApp.csproj "/bl:{}". The {} placeholder tells MSBuild to substitute a fresh, non-colliding filename automatically, so I never have to worry about overwriting a binlog from an earlier run or reusing one still open in another process.

results.content: Ran: dotnet build SimpleApp.csproj "/bl:{}" -> Build succeeded. A new *.binlog file (e.g. msbuild_1.binlog) was written to the working directory.

steps.message: Build succeeded and the binlog was written next to the project. I used /bl:{} on the build -- the {} placeholder makes MSBuild substitute a fresh, non-colliding filename automatically. I deliberately avoided bare /bl, since that always writes to msbuild.binlog and silently clobbers the previous build's log, and I avoided a hardcoded name like /bl:build.binlog since {} is available here and handles uniqueness for us.
